text: Juicy Broccoli (Japanese: , Jūshī Tomato, Juicy Tomato) are collectables in . They can be found on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, taking a bit releases their juices and they are a sweet and popular vegetable. Three are needed for Out-of-Luck Giorgio.

Kazat (Japanese: , Kairusu) is a Machina in . He is the father of Mixik and husband of Qofaria. He wants to be able to protect his family. He can be found at the entrance of the Hidden Machina Village on the Fallen Arm, from 06:00 to 18:00.

Karlos (Japanese: , Kararu) is a Homs in . He can be found near the entrance to the Hidden Machina Village on the Fallen Arm. He was presumed dead after the Battle of Sword Valley, but had actually landed by the Fallen Arm before being taken to the village. He is an old friend of Fiora's.
Kaelin (Japanese: , Kaito) is a pureblooded High Entia in . He can be found in the Great Hall in Alcamoth, next to the Ascension Hall transporter, from about 8:00 to 15:00.

Kaleka (Japanese: , Garuba) is a Nopon NPC in . He can be found north of the entrance to the Imperial Palace in Alcamoth at night. After the events at the Mechonis Core, he can be found near the Nopon Tower in Frontier Village at night. Kaleka is a deeply-rooted Alcamoth native, born into the ninth generation of a Nopon immigrant family. In the English language version of the game, Kaleka notably lacks any of the limited grammar speech patterns characteristic of Riki and most other Nopon, instead speaking in complete and well-articulated sentences with fully inflected articles, adverbs and first-, second- and third-person pronouns, and no "-pon" honorific suffixes or cute improvised adjectiv

Kacha (Japanese: ) is a Nopon in Xenoblade Chronicles. After Kacha's Kidnapping is complete, she can be found at the Nopon Merchant Camp in the middle of Lacus Swamp in Satorl Marsh, researching Giant ruins.

※ Bokoko will immediately give another quest after completing this quest. See Making Camp. ※ After this quest is completed, Kacha may offer another quest. See The Giants' Key. Kacha's Kidnapping (Japanese: , Sarawareta Kacha) is a quest in . It can be received from Bokoko at the Nopon Merchant Camp in Satorl Marsh. It is the first in a series of three quests involving Kacha and the Exile Fortress. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.
Juicy Melons (Japanese: , Mezumezumeron) are collectables in . They can be found in Sword Valley and Colony 6. According to their description, the juice inside them drips like water.
Jujube Silvers (Japanese: , Natsume Shirubā) are collectables in . They can be found in Sword Valley and Colony 6. According to their description, they are metallic flowers that grow on Mechonis.

Juicy Steakplants (Japanese: , Jūshii Makuwa) are collectables in . They can be found in Mechonis Field and Colony 6. According to their description, they do not look good but they taste nice and they look like meat when cut.
Ivy Nests (Japanese: , Shita no Su) are collectables in . They can be found in Mechonis Field and Colony 6. According to their description, they are nests for small animals made out of ivy.

Juicy Blueberries (Japanese: , Tajiru Burūberī) are collectables in . They can be found in Agniratha and Colony 6. According to their description, they are crammed full of juice and they are so good they melt someone's soul away.
Jungle Caps (Japanese: , Jango Kyappu) are light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are made from monster skin.
Itinerant Dorothea (Japanese: , Kariyado no Dorotēa) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Krabble family. It appears around Cliff Lake at level 6 during the daytime only.

Jungle Quadwings are enemies in . They are members of the Quadwing family, and can be found near the Waypoint Beacon in Makna Forest. They can be found perched on a climbable tree south of the waypoint. Five Jungle Quadwings must be defeated for the Makna Forest quest Monster Quest 1. They drop All-Seeing Eyes, which are required for the Frontier Village quest Secret Elixir Ingredients.

Kasharpa Falls (Japanese: , Kashuhaba no Taki) is a location in . It is located on the upper level of Bionis' Leg, between Bask Cave Passage and Believer's Paradise, and can be found by walking north from the Bask Cave Passage and swimming from there. Behind the waterfall itself, there is a small grotto in which a Key Item, the Kasharpa Water, can be found, required for Preparing for Adventure.
Jungle Bottoms are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Jail Bottoms are light legs armour in . They can be dropped by Racti Lexos and Plain Armus.
Jungle Gloves are light arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Terra Orluga, or be obtained as a quest reward.
Jail Tops are light torso armour in . It is part of the Jail set of armour along with the Jail Cap, Jail Gloves, Jail Bottoms and Jail Shoes.

Jabos Rock Rest Area (Japanese: , Jabosu-gan no Kyūkeijo) is a landmark in . It is located in Gaur Plain on the Bionis' Leg. It is a east of the exit from Ragrinar Canyon Path. A group of Armu can be found near here, as well as Fine Fliers by day. At night, Light Wisps will replace the Fine Fliers. Spear Tirkin can be found a small distance away from the landmark, in each diagonal compass direction except for the northwest.
Journey Diadems (Japanese: , Senri no Kanmuri) are medium head armour in . They are made from wood from Satorl Marsh.

※ After this quest is completed, Jackson may offer one of two mutually exclusive quests - either Jackson the Poet if the A route was taken or Jackson the Cook if the B route was taken. Also after this quest, Désirée may offer Désirée's Future. Jackson's Awakening (Japanese: , Jakuson no Kakusei) is a quest in . It can be received from Jackson in the alley in the southernmost area of the Residential District of Colony 9. If Melia is in the active party, she will comment.

Juicy Laia Fish are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from Laias in Eryth Sea, and are also available via trade in Alcamoth. According to their description, they produce copious meat juices that work well as a stock for other dishes. Three Juicy Laia Fish are needed for the quest Honouring the Nopon Sage.

The Junk Sword (Japanese: , Jankusōdo) is a weapon in . It is Shulk's initial weapon, a simple claymore he crafted himself. It is also the only weapon of Shulk's that is not a Monado. Due to this, the talent art is replaced with Turn Strike, an attack similar to Shaker Edge that inflicts Break. After Metal Face attacks Colony 9, the Junk Sword will be permanently replaced by the Monado, and cannot be re-equipped. This also means it is completely unavailable during New Game +.

Jack Knives (Japanese: , Jakkunaifu) are weapons in . They are Fiora's knives, and can be dropped by enemies in Tephra Cave or traded for with Désirée, if she becomes a sculpter after the quest Désirée's Future.
The Jaguar Lancer (Japanese: , Jagāransā) is a weapon in . It is one of Reyn's gunlances, and is dropped by practically all enemies below level 30 on the Bionis' Leg.
Jack Guarder (Japanese: , Jakkugādā) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn.
Jack Daggers (Japanese: , Shākudagā, Shark Dagger) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Fiora's twin blades, and can be dropped by enemies in the Central Factory.
Jumbo Guarders (Japanese: , Erefangādā, Elephant Guarder) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are gunlances wielded by Reyn.

Jackson the Poet (Japanese: , Shijin Jakuson) is a quest in . It can be received from Jackson in the alley at the southernmost area of Residential District in Colony 9. This quest does not become available until after Sharla has joined the party, but she does not have to be in the battle party. This quest and Jackson the Cook are mutually exclusive. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.
Kaboom Nibblers (Japanese: , Daibakuhatsu no Bakubaku) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are biters wielded by Riki. It can only be obtained by purchasing it at Colony 6 Shop 9 for 54,720 G
Jaw Nibblers (Japanese: , Kyōgaku no Bakubaku) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are biters that can be wielded by Riki. They can be obtained as a quest reward.
The Karma Blades (Japanese: , Karumaburēdo) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are twin blades wielded by Fiora, and can be dropped by enemies in Mechonis Field, or bought from several shops.

Jada Arachnos (Japanese: , Jada Supaido) are enemies in . They are members of the Arachno family, and can be found in Tephra Cave at levels 87 and 90, in a small room southwest of the Soothsayer's Crypt. They are smaller versions of Jadals Arachnos. They can be found only after Egil is defeated.

Jadals Arachnos (Japanese: , Jadarusu Supaido) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Arachno family, and can be found at levels 89 and 92 in Tephra Cave, southwest of the Soothsayer's Crypt in a small room. They are larger versions of Jada Arachnos. They also hatch in pairs of two at level 95 from the two Hanz Pods next to Plump Sprahda. They can only be found after the events at the Mechonis Core.
Kelsher Wetland (Japanese: , Kerusha Shitchi) is a landmark in . It is located in Satorl Marsh.
Kasharpa Water is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found at any time behind the Kasharpa Falls on Bionis' Leg. This item is required for Preparing for Adventure.

Judicious Bunnitzol (Japanese: , Senkoku no Banīdozuru) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Bunniv family, and can be found at level 94 in Tephra Cave. To find it, go to Heavenly Window, and go north down the hole. Afterwards head towards Forgotten Cave. This unique monster is only accessible after the events at Mechonis Core. It can drop the Bunniv Clubs needed for Friendship Tokens.

Itmos Upas (Japanese: , Itomusu Ūpā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Upa family, and can be found at level 30 in Makna Forest, near the Eks Watering Hole, between Bridge One and Great Makna Falls, or at the cove below the Divine Sanctuary. Defeating three of them is required to complete the Frontier Village's quest Monster Quest 1 - Part 1. Additionally, they can drop the Upa Embers needed for Material Quest 4.

Junk Krabbles (Japanese: , Janku Kuraibu) are enemies in . They are members of the Krabble family, and can be found at level 20 near Test Pit 2 in the Ether Mine. They are the only enemies that can drop Krabble Fixed Parts, which are needed for one route of Out Like a Light?.

Jackson the Cook (Japanese: , Ryōrinin Jakuson) is a quest in . It can be received from Jackson in the southwest portion of the Residential District of Colony 9. This quest and Jackson the Poet are mutually exclusive. If Dunban is in the active party, he will comment. At the very end of the quest, 100 reputation points are lost, so the total granted for this quest is 50.

Jaws of Death (Japanese: , Kyūshi Isatsu) is one of Dunban's arts in . It activates an aura that allows Dunban to recover HP after being incapacitated. It also replenishes his talent gauge by 50% and increases his physical arts damage by 50% for a duration.

Kamikaze Bune (Japanese: , Kamikaze no Bune) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a level 53 Mechon, and can be found on the north of the Control Tower in Sword Valley, on the top deck of the access bridge to Galahad Fortress. It is accompanied by two Offensive Mechon Plus.

Javelin Tirkins (Japanese: , Jaberin Tākin) are enemies in . They are members of the Tirkin family, and can be found at level 16 in Gaur Plain or at Tirkin Headquarters on Bionis' Leg. They can drop the Tirkin Crests needed for Material Quest 2.
Jelly Seluas (Japanese: , Jerī Serura) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Selua family, and can be found at levels 72 to 73 in the Bionis' Interior.
Jupiter (Japanese: , Kioku Kūkan - Mokusei) is a landmark in . It is a memory of Jupiter in Memory Space. The only enemy found here is Spirit - Xord, and there is a transporter to Mars.
The Key is a Key Item in . It is the object of Search Quest 3 in Colony 9. It can be found behind a house in the southeastern portion of the Residential District.

Kaleka's Repair Kit is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is given to the party by Kaleka during Broken Ether Furnace 2 in order to repair the Ether Furnace Controls and the transporters of Alcamoth.
The Judicial District is a location in . It is located on the third floor of Agniratha, opposite the Legislative District. The Sentimental Flamral, a Unique Monster, can be found here.

Jifum Beach (Japanese: , Jimufu no Hamabe) is a location in . It is a shore on the lower level of the Fallen Arm, on the east side of the Wreckage Beach. The Prosperous Zepar can be found here in the evening, as well as an Earth Ether Gear.
Just Like Old Times (Japanese: , Ano Koro no you ni) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at the Silver Wreckage on the Fallen Arm, between Fiora and Shulk at purple affinity.

Janpath Lake (English dub: ) (Japanese: , Janpasu-ko) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, east of New Los Angeles. It is surrounded by four plains, each named for its relative location to the lake (North Janpath Plain, South Janpath Plain, West Janpath Plain, and East Janpath Plain).

Javelins are melee weapons in . They are typically depicted as long metallic spears that can be thrown and used to jab at enemies. They are used by the Partisan Eagle and Astral Crusader Classes. When Astral Crusader is fully mastered, the Javelin becomes usable with any other class. Alexa, Bozé, Lao, and Liesel all wield Javelins, and Ga Buidhe is depicted using a similar weapon in combat.

The Jukebox is a special feature in the Collection Mode exclusive to (along with the Model Viewer), whereby the player can play musical tracks from the game at their leisure. With headphones plugged into the New 3DS, one can listen to the game's music while having the system closed in sleep mode. In the beginning, there are only a few tracks available, but as the player progresses through the story, more become available over the course of the game. Tracks are unlocked using tokens earned from the Music Raffle in Collection mode, and tokens can be earned in three ways: 3 for scanning the Shulk amiibo, 2 for every hit in StreetPass, and 1 for every 5 Play Coins exchanged. In addition, 10 toke

Juvenile Simius (Japanese: , Junia Shimiusu, Junior Simius) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Simius and can be found at level 9-17 or level 31-33 in Primordia. Five must be defeated to complete Primordia Trailblazing 2.

Junks Shop 1 is a shop in . It appears on the deck of Junks after the events at the Mechonis Core, and can be accessed in both the Hidden Machina Village and Colony 6, and later in the Bionis' Interior. It is operated by a Homs wearing a backpack, and sells weapons and arts manuals. He is accompanied by another Homs who operates Junks Shop 2, specialising in armour and arts manuals.

Junks Shop 2 is a shop in . It appears on the deck of Junks after the events at the Mechonis Core, and can be accessed in both the Hidden Machina Village and Colony 6, and later in the Bionis' Interior. It is operated by a Homs who sells armour and arts manuals. He is accompanied by another Homs wearing a backpack who operates Junks Shop 1, specialising in weapons and arts manuals.

Julius (Japanese: , Yuriusu) is a Human NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found along the south wall of BLADE Tower in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. He is a BLADE officer. After the Normal Mission Rescue at the Ensconced Citadel, he will be located on the north side of the Commercial District's West Melville Street until Going Viral is completed, after which he will be located next to the Mimeosome Maintenance Center in the Administrative District.

no5=KAKU-WEST＊→▲★★KAI is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles X, composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano. It is track five of disc one from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack, and the fifth part of the suite titled 0rCH-SUITE "X". The second half of this track is heard in the opening cutscenes, as the two alien factions are preparing to battle. The first half is later heard when Lao reveals himself as a spy for the Ganglion and steals the Prog Ares.
Jasper Incline (Japanese: , Hekigyoku no Saka) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Noctilum, northwest of Rustpool Banks.

Jocular Saltats (Japanese: , Fanī Sarutāto, Funny Saltat) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Saltats and can be found at level 12-14 around Rust Lake in Noctilum. Two are them must be hunted during the Basic Mission Sundering Saltats (Jocular). They drop Saltat Horns, one of which is needed to complete Indigen Investigation (Saltat Horn).

Jo (Japanese: , Ratte, Latte) is a NPC in . She can be found on Central Melville Street in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles, where she works as a barista. Coco is her boss. She has abysmal luck around machinery, as shown during the Normal Mission Better Latte Than Never.

Justin (Japanese: , Jasutin) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found near Barista Court in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles. He is a member of the Mediators Division. Justin is involved during the Normal Mission Rise of the Blood Lobster. Depending on the mission route chosen, he will either be dead or remain in the Ganglion Antropolis.

Jade Saltats (Japanese: , Jeido Sarutāto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Saltat family, and can be found at level 11-19 near Potter's Rock in Noctilum, inside a large red flower on top of a nearby trunk. It can sometimes be replaced by Jarosch, the Sensational.

Itinerant Saltats (Japanese: , Baguranto Sarutāto, Vagrant Saltat) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Saltat family, and can be found at level 26-28 on Oblivia's Great Washington Isle and around the Central Ibra Ravine fast travel point.

Javelin Insidias (Japanese: , Jaberin Parako) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Insidia family, and can be found at level 31-33 or at level 36-38 on Aaroy Plain, Ejiri Promontory, and South Coast in Oblivia. Five of these must be hunted to complete Ridding Insidias.

Jade Scirpos (Japanese: , Jeido Shirunea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Scirpo family and can be found at level 24-28 in the Castaway Cavern in Primordia. Five must be defeated during Squashing Scirpos.
Kent D. Carr (Japanese: , Kento D Kā) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Mimeosome Maintenance Center in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles.
Jetstream is a Debuff Art in . It inflicts Ether damage and the Stun effect to the target.

Jair Fortress (English dub: ) (Japanese: , Jaīru Yōsai) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Ganglion base located in Oblivia, on the east side of Sea Whisper Valley. FN Site 322 is located on the beach below it. Zo Zazhi must be spoken to and then fought here during A Dish Served Cold.
Jade Jaculs (Japanese: , Jeido Hasutara) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Jacul family, and can be found at level 38-39 at Shivering Sands in Sylvalum.
Jeffrey is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found near the Hangar in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles.

Jejebba (English dub: ) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Vitriol Cesspool in Noctilum. After completing Bozé's Ignorance, he can be found at the West Melville Street in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles, near the place where Bozé and Reggie can usually be found.

Keith (Japanese: , Kīsu) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at Biahno Lake in Primordia at anytime during Water Woes where it is required to meet him, after said mission he will be inside the Biahno Water-Purification Plant until Lakeside Getaway is accepted.
Jitsu (Japanese: , English dub: ) is an NPC in . He is a Nopon and can be found in the Whale's Nostril in Noctilum. He is met during the mission The Ties That Bind. He is a Tatsu's brother.
Jim is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found in the northwest part of the Commercial District in New Los Angeles. He is a member of the Mediators Division.
Kaisis (Japanese: , Kaishisu) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found in the northeast part of the Commercial District in New Los Angeles during the day along with Berry.
Jubietta is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found in the Central Industrial District of New Los Angeles during the day.
Jalimbo (Japanese: , Jirinbo) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Cathedral in the Residential District of New Los Angeles during the night.

Jajanni (English dub: ) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Starboard inside the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles, moving to and at the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District.
Jeshero is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found in the Starboard inside the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles.

Jagged Mortars (Japanese: , Gizagiza Suribachi) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, in particular near FN Site 111. Three pieces are needed for The Bug Whisperer.
Jobo Primroses (Japanese: , Jobo Matsuyoigusa) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia.
Jet Turtles (Japanese: , Jetto Tātoru) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia.

Izgnanie, the Smoldering (Japanese: , Sennetsu no Iguzunānye) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Lophid family. It can be found at level 64 at Sunset Falls in Cauldros above the lava falls. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Izgnanie, the Smoldering.

Keppo Carrots (English dub: , Japanese: , Kepo Ninjin) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, in particular east of Biahno Lake. Four of them are needed for Cooking Schooled.
Katoan Leaves (Japanese: , Katoa no Ha) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum. Ten must be gathered for Emergency Stores.

Kepha Hollies (Japanese: , Kefa Hiiragi) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in particular near FN Site 313, FN Site 314, FN Site 317, and FN Site 319. One is required for one route of Kidnapped: Uzoma Vassago.

Joadtanks (Japanese: , Jōdotanku) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum, in particular in the vicinity of the Divine Roost. Eight of them are required for BLADE Mission No. 16's Squad Task.
Jagitos Coppers (Japanese: , Jakitosu no Dō) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum. Ten are required during Pollution Solution.

Jagged Grex Tails are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Grexes, or for 30 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are one of the required components of Back Attack Plus and PositionDmg.BACK augments.
Joy is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found at the Sports Complex in the Residential District of New Los Angeles at daytime.
Ivory(Japanese: , Seborī) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is located near Deliverance Park in the Residential District of New Los Angeles.

Jindriska, the Serene (Japanese: , Seihitsu no Injushika) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Mortifole family. It can be found hidden at level 26 in Oblivia above the Twin Arches, south of the eastern arch.

Jarosch, the Sensational (, Kenran no Yarosuvaha) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Saltat family. It can be found at level 23 inside a large red flower on top of a tree trunk near Potter's Rock in Noctilum, rarely replacing the Jade Saltat that appears there.
Ji-ett, the Thunderclap (Japanese: , Jinrai no Ji-eto) is a Tyrant in . It is a Fal-swo machine. It can be found at level 72 in the sky above South Janpath BC in Primordia at night.
Judge Blattas (Japanese: , Jajji Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and can be found at level 41-50 in Primordia, near FN Site 108 during the day.
JD001: Juda (Japanese: , JD001: Juda) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Definian who appears in the Ganglion Antropolis in Cauldros during the Normal Mission Definian Downfall.

JS178: Jushe (Japanese: , JS178: Jashu) is a Mission Exclusive Secondary Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Definian and can be found at level 30 at Stoyanov Trail in Oblivia during the Normal Mission Sun'celeg Rises.

Judge Pugiliths (Japanese: , Jajji Berudero) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Pugilith machines, Ganglion's vehicles, and can be found at level 51-60 in the Ganglion Antropolis in Cauldros.
Jet Shrads (Japanese: , Jetto Zuttā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Shrad machines, and can be found at level 51-60 in Cauldros, southwest of FN Site 516.

Kan'tonam (Japanese: , Kan'otonamu) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is an Orphean who can be found at the BLADE Tower in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles, or at the Central Industrial District. He is also a BLADE and a member of the Reclaimers.

The Jacul Ire (Japanese: , Hasutara Būti, Jacul Booty) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Jacul family, and can be found at level 32 at the south-western edge of Lake Ciel in Sylvalum. Battling it is required during Castle in the Sky in order to retrieve the Kuta's Cargo.
Jalolo is a Nopon NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found in Dopang Caravan near the Cleansing Spring in Sylvalum during the night after Castle in the Sky is completed.
Jacul Jaunt is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Interceptors and the primary destination is Cauldros.
Juicy Analysis is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from BLADE HQ to obtain Intelligent Liquid Metal in Sylvalum.
Jacul Horns are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Jaculs.
Jacul Waterfall Orbs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Jaculs.
Jacul A is a Holofigure in . It depicts a blue jacul variant. It can be obtained from Jia Mian, the Beloved in Cauldros.
Jacul B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a green jacul variant. It can be obtained from silver drops from Radovan, the Sky Baron in Sylvalum.

Just Married is a special Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a recently married Tree Clan Prone couple, a male with a female Tree Clan Prone on his shoulder. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission A Grim Undertaking.

Iyst Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts an Orphean Technologies Knife. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission House Call. The Iyst weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Iyst * Iron Iyst * Carbide Iyst * Cermet Iyst * Chrome Iyst * Chromoly Iyst * Cobalt Iyst * Original Iyst * Titaniym Iyst * Ceramic Iyst * Diamond Iyst * Ultra Diamond Iyst

Iyst II Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts an Orphean Technologies Knife. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Lone Survivors. The Iyst II weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Iyst II * Iron Iyst II * Carbide Iyst II * Cermet Iyst II * Chrome Iyst II * Chromoly Iyst II * Cobalt Iyst II * Titanium Iyst II * Ceramic Iyst II * Diamond Iyst II

Jyth Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts an Orphean Technologies Javelin. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission The Journey Begins. The Jyth weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Jyth * Iron Jyth * Carbide Jyth * Cermet Jyth * Chrome Jyth * Chromoly Jyth * Cobalt Jyth * Titanium Jyth * Original Jyth * Ceramic Jyth * Diamond Jyth

Jacul Nest is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.10, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting ten Petramands. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Keep Out! is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.18, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twenty-four Jaculs. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Jet Black Devil Wings are a casual head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They have the same appearance on all characters, and share this appearance with the other Devil Wings headgear.
Jamming is a skell armor antidamage augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell evasion against homing attacks by 10% to 50%.
Jeans are Casual Wear leg armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Jackets are Casual Wear upper-body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.

Juicy Wild Meats are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Stella Eks in Eryth Sea, or traded for in Eryth Sea and Alcamoth. According to their description, they are monster meats melt in the mouth that taste best as they are swallowed. Three are needed for Cook-Off Counter Attack!.

Kattl Krabbles (Japanese: , Kattā Kuraibu) are enemies in . They are members of the Krabble family, and can be found at level 1 on the Goldmouth Exit Dock in the Argentum Trade Guild. This enemy drops no items.

Jac is a Gormotti in . He hails from Torigoth, and his goal is to become a Driver so he can earn money for his family after his parents left. After the party arrives in Torigoth, he tries to summon a Blade by touching a Core Crystal, against the wishes of his younger siblings, Morca, Zelen, and Neel. They were worried he didn't have the aptitude to become a driver. He is originally pushed aside by a much larger, more overconfident man who ends up failing to resonate with the crystal. Jac succeeds instead, much to everyone's joy, and goes to Mor Ardain to join the Ardainian army after training. Jac can later be found in Alba Cavanich along with Yachik, his Blade, dressed as an official soldie

Five Jenerossi Teas can be received for free if the Expansion Pass has been bought.

The Crimson Orchid Brighid DLC Aux Core has an equivalent effect, which is functionally identical to the Affinity MAX Evade V Aux Core.
